pricing.summary: This page compares providers’ public list prices for sandbox use, idle time and storage.
pricing.title: Provider Pricing

active-use.caption: Bars show price per active hour (USD). Lower is better.
active-use.how_it_is_measured: Separate per-second CPU and memory rates are added and multiplied by 3600 seconds per hour.
active-use.how_to_read: A range shows the lowest and highest published prices for the same configuration.
limits: The comparison excludes discounts, credits, plan fees.
active-use.summary: The hourly price for an active sandbox is based on published CPU and memory rates.
active-use.title: Active Use

disk-storage.caption: Bars show price (USD/GiB-month). Lower is better.
disk-storage.how_it_is_measured: Storage list prices are normalized to the comparison unit while the table retains the original source unit.
disk-storage.how_to_read: The table shows the provider’s quoted unit; the chart uses the normalized comparison unit.
limits: The listed rate does not establish whether a particular snapshot or volume is billable.
disk-storage.summary: The price for keeping disks, snapshots and volumes is the provider’s published storage charge.
disk-storage.title: Disk Storage

image-storage.caption: Bars show price (USD/GiB-month). Lower is better.
image-storage.how_it_is_measured: Storage list prices are normalized to the comparison unit while the table retains the original source unit.
image-storage.how_to_read: The table shows the provider’s quoted unit; the chart uses the normalized comparison unit.
limits: The listed rate does not establish whether a particular snapshot or volume is billable.
image-storage.summary: The price for keeping stored images is the provider’s published storage charge.
image-storage.title: Image Storage

inactive-use.caption: Bars show price per hour (USD) at {idle}% idle and {paused}% paused. Lower is better.
inactive-use.how_it_is_measured: Each state’s hourly price is weighted by its selected time share before the rates are combined.
inactive-use.how_to_read: Set the share of time spent in each state to compare its effect on the charge.
limits: The comparison excludes discounts, credits, plan fees.
inactive-use.summary: Idle and paused billing rules determine the listed cost when a sandbox is inactive.
inactive-use.title: Inactive Use

billed_on.answer: $0.80 per vCPU-month and $0.70 per GB-month of allocated RAM while running, plus $0.09 per GB-month of reserved disk in every state; a month is 730 hours, metered per minute.

ends.answer: At delete, which settles the final minutes. Measured, the last part minute before delete was billed in full.

extra_charges.answer: Managed LLM, search and tool calls debit the same wallet per instance within a budget that defaults to $0. Performance instances bill compute at 4x and VM instances at 2.5x. Backups and egress are not priced on the pages checked.

idle_and_paused.answer: Running and the transitional states bill the full rate; sleeping, stopped and waking bill disk only. A stopped instance measured billed disk alone. A sleeper parked in cold storage bills its compressed bytes at a separate rate.

image_pull.answer: Not stated. The meter starts at running, so a create that fails costs nothing; two measured creates of the default template returned in under a second.

left_out.answer: Managed LLM, search and tool spend (the instance's other usage fields), Performance instances, cold-storage time, backups, egress, the sign-up credit and top-ups.

per_sandbox_data.answer: Yes. GET /v1/usage lists each instance's spend in micro-dollars over up to 90 days, deleted ones included; compute lands within the hour and, measured, at delete.

rounding.answer: Each period is billed in whole minutes, rounded up, and the next state starts at the end of the last billed minute; each settled debit is a whole micro-dollar.

starts.answer: When the instance first reaches running; nothing is debited at create. Measured, the first billed minute began at the instance's created second, before create returned.

billed_on.answer: Memory allocated at creation, per GB-second. CPU is not charged separately; it is allocated from the memory size. Our 4096 MiB sandbox was billed as 4 GB.

ends.answer: Measured at destroy returned. Destroy sent is ruled out, as it would make the batch 1.8% shorter than billed.

extra_charges.answer: Snapshots $0.20, deployment images $0.045 and volumes $0.12, each per GiB-month. The sandbox's own disk has no separate charge, because its writable layer lives in the allocated memory that is billed. No creation fee or GPU price is stated. Egress is listed as included.

idle_and_paused.answer: Active is billed. Without an active connection a sandbox enters standby, where memory is not billed but snapshot storage is. Blaxel's pages say about 5 s or 15 s to standby, and we measured 22.7 to 34.8 s. Archived is "you stop paying for it". Paused and stopped are not stated.

image_pull.answer: Unknown for a cold, large custom image; not stated. Our check used a cached standard image and Blaxel's base image (creates took 0.2 to 0.4 s, one 2.13 s). A brought image must be built in the workspace.
image_pull.unknown_how: Build a large custom image in the workspace, create sandboxes from it and compare billed seconds with create sent and create returned.

left_out.answer: Up to $200 free credits, tier top-ups (prepaid usage), support add-ons, custom domains, image and volume storage, and taxes. Standby snapshot storage is included in the reported cost. Whether free credit is drawn at list rates is not stated.

per_sandbox_data.answer: Yes. The metrics API gives each sandbox's cost by billing dimension, in hourly buckets at finest. Blaxel says figures take "a few minutes, sometimes longer". Ours appeared about 50 s after create and were final 45 to 113 s after destroy, then unchanged for over 30 minutes. Read every page of the response.

rounding.answer: Compute in whole seconds, truncated; every compute cost was a whole number of seconds at the list rate. Standby snapshot storage is added per second, so a total is not always whole seconds. No minimum or increment is stated on the pricing page.

starts.answer: Measured at create returned. Create sent is not ruled out for creates of 0.2 to 0.4 s; the one 2.13 s create fitted create returned only.

providers.basis: a flat rate per sandbox size

billed_on.answer: Billable machine-seconds, weighted by size multiplier (0.5, 1, 2, 50/9 for small, default, large, xlarge), at $0.036 per hour of default size (secondsPerDollar 100000), while the sandbox runs. Published as a flat per-hour rate per size: small $0.018, default $0.036, large $0.072, xlarge $0.200. No size has a GPU.

ends.answer: A stop ends machine billing: stopped time is never counted, and time past a refused stop is excluded. Auto-stop ends a sandbox after its deadline (1 hour by default).

extra_charges.answer: Extra starts cost $0.03 to $0.07 each. Create, fork and resume count. The wallet pays first. An opted-in invoice can pay when the wallet is empty. Extra saved snapshots cost $0.056 each per day. The AI proxy costs $1 per enabled day plus $1 per 1,000 requests. Snapshot and proxy charges draw from the wallet. Egress is free.

idle_and_paused.answer: There is no pause; an idle sandbox bills as running until it stops or auto-stops. A stopped sandbox costs no machine time and keeps its disk free for at least 14 days. After that it is eligible for automated retention cleanup. The provider currently documents the production cleanup job as reporting candidates without deleting them.

image_pull.answer: Not stated; environment or image load time is not broken out on the billing pages.
image_pull.unknown_how: Compare billable seconds for a sandbox created from a cold environment against a cached one at known durations.

left_out.answer: Plan commitments ($20/$100/$500/$2000 per month per seat, returned as VM time at list rates), included starts and concurrency limits, the wallet bonus of 2% to 25% on payments of $200 or more, the 7-day free trial's limits, the $100-plan requirement for xlarge, and taxes.

per_sandbox_data.answer: GET /sandboxes/{id}/usage reports weighted seconds, list-priced dollars, running state and the size. After deletion the sandbox's usage record is unavailable. The last pre-delete read may omit time before deletion. List include=cost returns an aggregate deletedCost, without a per-sandbox breakdown.

rounding.answer: Billed per second. The usage API returns whole billable machine-seconds and dollars to six decimals; no minimum duration or rounding increment is published.

starts.answer: Not stated where the meter starts inside a create, resume or fork call. The usage record's seconds is the billed quantity, so the edge is Boat's own meter, not a call boundary.

billed_on.answer: $0.047 per vCPU-hour of CPU time used, $0.014 per GiB-hour of resident RAM while running or in standby, and $0.000096 per GiB-hour of written disk in every state; never provisioned size.

ends.answer: Hibernated and stopped machines still bill written disk; stopping alone does not end all charges. Exact deletion billing edges are not stated by the provider.

extra_charges.answer: State transitions cost nothing; separate snapshot and custom-domain fees are not stated by the provider on the checked pricing pages. Do not treat unpublished fees as zero.

idle_and_paused.answer: Idle CPU bills only time used; standby or suspend-to-RAM bills resident RAM and written disk. Hibernation and stopped machines bill written disk only; generic paused represents standby, not hibernation.

image_pull.answer: Not stated whether image pull and restore work is included in the machine meter.
image_pull.unknown_how: Compare provider usage records for cold and cached images, without substituting call duration.

left_out.answer: No monthly plan, paid-plan minimum or per-seat fee is published for pay as you go. Credits, taxes, custom pricing and annual self-host licences are outside the per-machine USD list cost.

per_sandbox_data.answer: machines.usage(id) returns machine_id, currency, cost_micro, complete, usage quantities and rates; the SDK calls cost_micro an estimate at current rates, not the invoiced settlement. Accept only complete USD records whose identity and rates match.

rounding.answer: Metered every second, settled every 15 minutes, with no minimum per machine. Each organization settlement rounds each resource up to the next millionth of its currency; this is not per-machine rounding.

starts.answer: Not stated where metering begins within create or resume calls; only the provider's usage record supplies cost.

rounding.answer: Not stated beyond "calculated per second". Billed periods have millisecond edges, and a 247 ms period was priced at its exact length.

starts.answer: At create returned, measured on seven sandboxes. Daytona's first period began 14 to 86 ms earlier, within network and clock error.

billed_on.answer: vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds of memory as allocated, while running. Disk is included in the plan (10 GiB Hobby, 20 GiB Pro), not a meter. Sandboxes are CPU-only.

ends.answer: Billing stops immediately on pause, kill or timeout. The calculator uses the killed event, which fell inside the destroy call on five sandboxes.

extra_charges.answer: None published: no creation fee, no paused-state or template storage charge. Network is not mentioned on the pricing or billing pages.

idle_and_paused.answer: Only running time is billed. Paused sandboxes are kept with no time limit and are not billed. Whether pausing itself is billed has not been tested.

image_pull.answer: Not stated. A cold large image's created event came 9.7 s after create was sent, inside the create call; we did not isolate an image-load charge.

left_out.answer: Plan fees (Pro $150 per month, concurrency add-ons, Enterprise minimum), the one-time $100 Hobby credit and taxes. Plans cap vCPU and memory (8 each), and runtime (1 hour Hobby, 24 hours Pro).

per_sandbox_data.answer: No cost. Killed and paused events, from the events API or webhooks, carry the allocated vCPUs, memory and runtime. The console's usage tab shows totals only. The first killed event arrived within 15 s. Running time comes from event timestamps, not execution_time, which can under-report after a snapshot.

rounding.answer: Billed per second. No minimum duration or rounding increment is published.

starts.answer: Not stated. The calculator uses E2B's created event, which fell inside the create call on five sandboxes. This does not show E2B bills from it.

providers.basis: the larger of request and use CPU and memory

billed_on.answer: CPU (physical cores, 1 core = 2 vCPUs) and memory (GiB), each on the larger of requested and actual use. No sandbox cost is calculated from the request. Minimum request 0.125 cores and 128 MiB.

ends.answer: At Modal's finished_at, measured on 325 one-sandbox Apps; each App's bill stopped growing then, and its final rows appeared within 315 seconds. The exact edge and rounding are unsettled, as the median bill was 2.22 seconds below created_at to finished_at at list rates.

extra_charges.answer: Region multiplier on CPU, memory and GPU of 1.15 (broad region) or 1.75 (narrow region). Egress $0.04 per GiB above a workspace allowance, billed from 2026-10-01. Volumes $0.09 per GiB-month. GPUs per second by model. No snapshot or image storage price is stated.

idle_and_paused.answer: Not stated for sandboxes. The pricing page bills a 60-second default keep-alive for applications that take inputs, but does not say whether it applies to sandboxes. Sandboxes have a timeout (5 minutes by default, up to 24 hours) and an optional idle timeout, neither tied to billing. We have not measured this.

image_pull.answer: Modal's pages do not say. In our check, five cold images with pulls of 20 to 133 s were not billed (620 s billed against 611 s from create returned and 1,016 s from create sent).

left_out.answer: Plan fees (Starter $0, Team $250 per month), monthly free credits, credit programs, discounts, taxes, and the egress allowance. The list-price figure also leaves out volumes, snapshot retention and egress.

per_sandbox_data.answer: Workspace.billing.report gives each App's hourly USD total and its cost per resource, with no sandbox ID. The recorded request window lets us identify covered hours with no returned row. Rows stayed readable after the App stopped, so stop each App to stay within the 200 deployed Apps a workspace allows. Retention past 2 h 5 min is untested.

rounding.answer: Billed per second, and Modal's billing page lists no minimum time increment. How a partial second is rounded is not stated.

starts.answer: Measured on 2026-10-11, not complete. Billing starts at about when Modal sets the sandbox's creation time, 20 to 70 ms before the create call returns. It does not start when the call is sent.

billed_on.answer: Memory as provisioned (2 GB per vCPU), CPU as active use (I/O wait is not counted). Whether Active CPU is per vCPU or per sandbox, and whether GB is 1,000 or 1,024 MB, is not stated.

ends.answer: Not stated. In five samples stoppedAt came before our destroy call and duration equalled stoppedAt minus startedAt; no bill was compared.

extra_charges.answer: Creation $0.60 per million. Network: data sent out and all exposed-port traffic, $0.15 per GB in iad1. Snapshots $0.08 per GB-month. Disk (64 GB) is included. Not stated: GPU.

idle_and_paused.answer: Not stated for starting, stopping or stopped sessions. A stopped persistent sandbox keeps a snapshot, billed as snapshot storage; deleting the sandbox does not delete it.

image_pull.answer: Not stated. Creation waits until the sandbox is ready, and restoring an uncached snapshot is included in creation time. We did not test cold against cached images.

left_out.answer: Plan fees and allowances, other regions than iad1, enterprise pricing, taxes, Drives, container registry storage and the snapshot kept after the last stop (30 days after last use by default).

per_sandbox_data.answer: Usage per session after a clean stop: duration, activeCpuDurationMs, network bytes, sizeBytes for snapshots. No cost per sandbox; charges are per project per day. Not stated: delay or retention.

rounding.answer: Provisioned memory is billed in 1-minute minimum increments. No rule is published for Active CPU. Creations are counted per call.

starts.answer: Not stated. In five samples the session startedAt fell inside our create call; no bill was compared.
